summary: At 6,339 square miles — larger than Connecticut — Siskiyou County holds barely 42,500 people, making it one of the most sparsely populated places in California at just seven residents per square mile, a density that redefines what "neighbor" means. The landscape earns that emptiness: 14,179-foot Mount Shasta dominates the southern horizon, the Marble Mountains and Trinity Alps carve the west, and the Klamath River threads through deep canyons toward the coast. This is not commuter territory — the economy runs on timber, ranching, healthcare at a few small hospitals, and public-sector jobs, with College of the Siskiyous in Weed providing a modest educational anchor. A median home price of $284,500 against a median household income of $55,499 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.1, affordable by California standards but tighter than it first appears given a 16.6% poverty rate that signals an economy with limited high-wage rungs to climb. Winters average lows near 39°F with genuine snow at elevation, while summers deliver long, dry days across 8.5 hours of annual average sunshine — ideal for the fishing, hiking, and backcountry access that define daily life more than any restaurant strip or retail corridor. Siskiyou is essentially a place where the land is the infrastructure, and the tradeoff for extraordinary natural access is an economy that asks you to arrive with your livelihood already figured out.
